about: The card-only recipes of the image and edit routes: which (route, family, quant) may run across two cards, which loader puts which weight on which card, and the per-card VRAM peak a call is held to. cuda:0 is the STORAGE card (text encoder, VAE, the donor blocks of the DiT), cuda:1 the COMPUTE card (the DiT's resident share and the sampler's activations); render/multicard-recipes.mjs reads this file and internal/hostneed keeps a copy of the figures (a Go test pins the two). maxPixels, when present, is the largest canvas (width times height, in pixels) a call on the row may ask for, and maxPixelsNote says where the number comes from; the runner refuses a larger canvas by name (canvasRefusal), where maxMegapixels is the edit canvas the compute peak was scaled to (the edit runner refuses a pinned canvas above it). blocked, when present, is a sentence: the row exists but the runner refuses it by name until the thing it says was run is run (a held-back row is no recipe to the estimate, the doctor and the typed doors; its data stays for the proof arm). basis is 'measured' only for a row whose per-card peak was read in a run that used the read-only safetensors loader (a card-only run that charged no weights to host commit); every image arm of the 2026-10-11 two-card benchmark ran the stock loader, so those rows are 'predicted' and a call on them declares the ordinary estimate until a live run with the read-only loader promotes them.

rows.blocked: the card-only placement puts this recipe's int8 DiT on cuda:1, and no run has: the benchmark arms the row cites ran the int8 DiT on cuda:0 with the bf16 text encoder on cuda:1, the reverse. A comfy_kitchen int8 model run through ComfyUI-MultiGPU with the compute device off cuda:0 is a recorded illegal memory access in the int8 dispatch path (upstream issue 220, unfixed; it is why the pooled LTX-2.5 seat keeps compute cuda:0). Run one int8 arm with the DiT on cuda:1, then clear "blocked" on this row in render/multicard-recipes.json and Blocked in internal/mediacap/multicard.go; the bf16 DiT row of this family is held back too (the 16.33 GiB bf16 text encoder this row also names cannot be built on the storage card), so lifting this row needs that fixed as well, and no qwen-image-2.1 file has a card-only recipe today
rows.evidence: Benchmark 2026-10-11, qwen-image-2.1 int8_convrot DiT with the bf16 text encoder at 2048x2048, 40 steps: two plain pins 213.4 s and the text-encoder layer split 215.1 s against 238.4 s on one card, pixel-identical to the single-card render (max abs diff 0); per-card peaks 13.55 GiB on the card that held the text encoder and 8.89 GiB on the card that held the DiT. The arms ran the stock loader, and the split's allocation string was not recorded, so the 5 GiB share of the text encoder on the compute card is this file's choice (11.3 GiB of the 16.3 GiB encoder stays on the storage card, beside the VAE).

rows.blocked: under --gpu-only ComfyUI builds the whole 16.33 GiB bf16 text encoder on the storage card (cuda:0, a 15.9 GiB card) before the DisTorch2 allocation that splits it is applied, so a live card-only run of this recipe ran out of memory 1.4 s in, with 14.10 GiB allocated, while the encoder was still being built; no resident share or peak figure in this row changes that. A loader that builds the text encoder per card, or one measured arm that fits the pair, lifts it: then clear blocked on this row in render/multicard-recipes.json and Blocked in internal/mediacap/multicard.go
rows.evidence: Benchmark 2026-10-11, bf16 DiT (13.3 GiB): all-VRAM across two cards 357.5 s against 356 s on the lane's prior, pixel-identical to the single-card render; two plain pins still offloaded 1.5 GiB of the DiT to RAM (380.9 s), which is why the DiT is split by allocation here. That all-VRAM arm used the display card as the donor; no arm ran this split on two non-display cards, so the 8 GiB resident share is arithmetic (compute 8 + 2.5 activations + 0.3 context; storage the 13.3 GiB text-encoder share + VAE + context at the text-encode stage) and the peaks are predicted. Correction, 0.182.1: the 13.3 GiB text-encoder share above is the size of the bf16 DiT file (13.25 GiB), not of the encoder, which is 16.33 GiB (11.3 GiB after a 5 GiB resident share); and a live card-only run never reached the sampler, because ComfyUI builds the whole encoder on the storage card before the split applies (see blocked).

rows.maxPixelsNote: the first live two-card run of this recipe, at 928x1664 (1.54 MP), ran out of memory in the sampler, and no canvas of this row has been measured: the cap is chosen, not measured
rows.evidence: 2512 bf16 (38 GiB) fits no card, so 2512 is the Q5_1 GGUF (14.3 GiB). No 2512 arm ran on two cards; the same-size 2511 Q5_1 GGUF did (edit-gguf-full on two cards: all 14.3 GiB on the storage card left 0.3 GiB free there), and the benchmark predicted a 3 GiB resident share of the DiT on the compute card (storage about 12.6 GiB, compute about 4.9 GiB) without running it. The fp8 text encoder stays whole on the storage card. Canvas cap (maxPixels 1472700, 1.47 MP): chosen, not measured. The row's first live two-card run, at 928x1664 (1.54 MP) with the 3 GiB resident share, ran out of memory in the sampler (torch OutOfMemoryError on device 0, the storage card, 56 s in), so the figures above do not hold at that canvas, and no 2512 canvas has been measured on two cards. 1.47 MP is the largest canvas the evidence shows a same-size Q5_1 GGUF running on two cards (the 2511 edit below, every weight on the storage card), and it sits below the canvas that failed; the qwen-image default canvas (1328x1328, 1.76 MP) is above it, so a call that names no size is refused too. A measured arm at a larger canvas, or a re-split that fits 928x1664, replaces the cap.

rows.maxPixelsNote: chosen, not measured: 1.5 MP (1024x1536); the default 1024x1024 is inside it, the 2048x1024 bake-off canvas is not
rows.evidence: The bf16 DiT (24.5 GiB) with the Qwen3-VL-4B bf16 text encoder (8.3 GiB) is 33 GiB of weights, more than one card and less than the pair. 12 GiB of the DiT stays on the compute card (12 + 2.0 activations at 1024x1024 + 0.3 context = 14.3 GiB) and the other 12.5 GiB on the storage card beside the VAE (13.7 GiB with decode headroom). The text encoder is built whole on the storage card at the text-encode stage (8.3 + VAE + context, about 9 GiB) and freed before the DiT's donor blocks land, as the fp8 Qwen2.5-VL encoder of the 2511 edit was in the 2026-10-11 two-card benchmark under --gpu-only and --cache-none. Predicted from that run and the September pooled krea2 renders, not yet run card-only.

Benchmark 2026-10-11, section 4.6: fp8mixed (19.1 GiB) at 1.47 MP on two 5060 Ti with the read-only loader, compute card 9 GiB resident, 10.1 GiB on the storage card, bypass LoRA: success in 145.5 s (9.4 s per step), peaks 11.9 GiB on the compute card and 10.9 GiB on the storage card, host growth 1.87 GiB. The figures here are the compute peak scaled to the 2.0 MP cap of the edit canvas (activations 2.6 GiB at 1.47 MP, 3.5 at 2.0) and the storage peak rounded up. One card cannot hold the model (OOM at the load), the merging LoRA loader ran out of memory, so the bypass loader is part of the recipe.

Benchmark 2026-10-11, section 4.6: Q5_1 GGUF at 1.47 MP on two 5060 Ti with every weight on the storage card: success in 192.3 s but only 0.3 GiB free there, 'too thin for production'; the benchmark's own prediction for a 3 GiB resident share on the compute card is storage about 12.6 GiB and compute about 4.9 GiB at that 1.47 MP canvas, not run. The compute figure here is scaled to the 2.0 MP cap this row claims, as the fp8mixed row's is: the 1.9 GiB the compute card held at 1.4727 MP grows to 2.6 GiB, so 3 + 2.6 = 5.6 GiB. The run used the read-only loader (host growth 1.50 GiB).
